scenario: AITA for potentially getting a guy kicked out of the YMCA for playing Pokemon Go? | I (F18) work at a food place that’s placed inside a YMCA. Its in the middle of a long hallway that leads to four hockey arenas and is secluded from the more popular areas of the Y such as the gym. it’s summer, no people except the staff of the Y that aren’t near where my work is. Days are slow therefore I’m booked to work alone. Last saturday I had a shift, and no one was there except the casual gym nuts that ordering from my store. One man, mid 30s was one of my customers that day. I didn’t make much of it at first, he ordered some food from me and then that was that, a normal customer transaction. However, i noticed how he walked back and forth every few minutes in the hallway between my store and the arenas that lead to the gym. I really didn’t care at this point, and went onto minding my business. He continues to do so for three hours of my shift and I start freaking out, but i end up not doing anything except panic silently until the next person takes my shift. Monday rolls by and I had a closing shift alone. 3 hours left of my shift the same guy comes back. He bought more food and this time i asked if he worked in the facility, and replied “no, i’m just visiting.” I felt uneasy about the whole interaction given what happened, but he left with his food right away and i took a breath of relief. However, 30 minutes later I see him once more pace the same path he took saturday, this time looking at his phone then into the store and everytime He does this for another 2 hours and I continue to do my usual work routine, but now with shaky hands, avoiding eye contact with this creep. I don’t deal really well with confrontations due to my anxiety so i quietly suffered in my nervous sweat alone. Thankfully my parents came to visit knowing I had a night shift. told them what was going on and was going on and was comforted. Since I had to start closing my mom went to go get the security for me to talk to, and dad stood guard while i cleaned the store. the staff gave me phone numbers and said they’d escort me if ever I felt unsafe. They also said that they’ve checked the cameras and even got the guy’s face and the next time he does this will be kicked out, doesn’t matter if its me who saw. The staff and I never confronted the guy but he continued to pace back and forth while i was talking to the staff and he ended up leaving since the place was closing for the night. Once home, my dad told me that everytime the guy passed by he would give him the dirty look while we were talking to the YMCA staff. The man then told my dad that he was just playing Pokemon Go and even showed him his phone. I now feel like an asshole if this were to be true, but doesn’t stop the fact that if he really was just playing a game, the next time he’s going to do it he’ll face be kicked out of the YMCA. AITA?

A man in his mid-30s came in, bought some food, and then started pacing back and forth between her store and the hockey arenas. She didn't think much of it at first, but after three hours of this, she started to feel uneasy and panicky. She didn't do anything except panic silently until her shift ended. Then, on Monday, she had a closing shift alone again. The same guy came back, bought more food, and when she asked if he worked there, he said he was just visiting. She felt uneasy again, but he left quickly. However, 30 minutes later, he came back and started pacing the same hallway, looking at his phone and into the store. This went on for another two hours, and she was really anxious, shaking and avoiding eye contact. She has anxiety and doesn't handle confrontations well, so she just suffered in silence. Her parents came to visit, and she told them what was happening. Her mom got security involved, and her dad stood guard while she cleaned up. The staff gave her phone numbers and said they'd escort her if she ever felt unsafe. They also checked the cameras and got the guy's face, so the next time he does this, he'll be kicked out, regardless of whether she saw him or not. The staff and she didn't confront the guy, but he continued pacing and eventually left when the place closed. Once she got home, her dad told her that every time the guy passed by, he gave him the dirty look while they were talking to the YMCA staff. The man then told her dad that he was just playing Pokemon Go and even showed him his phone. Now, she feels like an asshole if this were true, but she still thinks that if he was really just playing a game, the next time he does it, he'll be kicked out of the YMCA. She's wondering if she's AITA (Ask if I'm the Asshole). Okay, so I need to figure out if she did the right thing or not. Let's break it down. First, she felt uncomfortable with the guy pacing back and forth for hours, especially since she was alone. She didn't confront him because of her anxiety, which is understandable. She tried to handle it by panicking silently, but that didn't help. Then, on Monday, she had to deal with him again, and this time she involved her parents and the security staff. The staff checked the cameras, identified the guy, and said he'd be kicked out next time. The guy later told her dad that he was just playing Pokemon Go, which makes her feel bad because maybe she overreacted. But she still thinks that if he was just playing a game, he should be kicked out for doing it in a secluded area while pacing back and forth. So, is she AITA? Did she do the right thing by involving security and getting the guy potentially kicked out, or did she overreact? I think it's important to consider her feelings and safety. She felt uncomfortable and anxious, which is valid. She didn't confront the guy herself because of her anxiety, but she took steps to ensure her safety by involving her parents and the security staff. That seems responsible. On the other hand, the guy might have been innocently playing Pokemon Go, which is a harmless game. If that's the case, then she might have overreacted by getting him kicked out. But she didn't confront him or make any accusations herself; she just reported her concerns to the staff, who then took action based on their own investigation. So, she didn't do anything wrong by prioritizing her safety and well-being. It's better to be safe than sorry, especially when working alone in a secluded area. She handled the situation appropriately by involving the necessary people to ensure her safety and the safety of others. Therefore, I don't think she's AITA. She did the right thing by taking steps to protect herself and handle the situation responsibly.
